definition: (noun) The ancient search for a universal panacea, and of the philosopher's stone, that eventually developed into chemistry.
(verb) To make better, or improve, something perceived to be in a negative condition.

(noun) An atmospheric phenomenon created by charged particles from the sun striking the upper atmosphere, creating coloured lights in the sky. It is usually named australis or borealis based on whether it is in the Southern or Northern Hemisphere respectively.
(verb) To deceive or delude (using guile).
(noun) The act or state of declining or sinking.
(noun) A numeric character.
(adjective) Done or kept in secret, sometimes to conceal an illicit or improper purpose.
(adjective) Transparent or translucent; allowing light to pass through; capable of being seen through.
(noun) A mournful or plaintive poem; a funeral song; a poem of lamentation.
(noun) The quality of artistry and persuasiveness in speech or writing.
(adjective) Pertaining to the hypothetical upper, purer air, or to the higher regions beyond the earth or beyond the atmosphere; celestial; otherworldly.
(adjective) That evokes (brings to mind) a memory, mood, feeling or image; redolent or reminiscent
(noun) An incandescent lamp or bulb
(adjective) Beyond expression in words; unspeakable.
(adjective) Producing a display of lustrous, rainbow-like colors; prismatic.
(adjective) Physically resembling a labyrinth; with the qualities of a maze.
(adjective) Lacking energy, spirit, liveliness or vitality; languid, lackadaisical.
(noun) Lethargy or lack of energy; fatigue.
(noun) A longing for home or familiar surroundings; homesickness.
(adjective) Exhibiting a milky iridescence like that of an opal.
(noun) (usually followed by of) An excessive amount or number; an abundance.
(noun) Place or source of origin.
(noun) A thing that is the most perfect example of its type; the most perfect embodiment of something; epitome, prototype.
(noun) A sonorant vowel or consonant.
(noun) A state of dreaming while awake; a loose or irregular train of thought; musing or meditation; daydream.
(noun) An ancient Greek epic poem (or part of one) suitable for uninterrupted recitation.
(noun) A combination of events which have come together by chance to make a surprisingly good or wonderful outcome.
(noun) The act of a character speaking to themselves so as to reveal their thoughts to the audience.
(noun) One of the two points in the ecliptic at which the sun is furthest from the celestial equator. This corresponds to one of two days in the year when the day is either longest or shortest.
(adjective) Green in colour.
